description: Cross Peterborough's railway story, a museum that became an infirmary and an Art Deco outdoor pool before a former technical college serves the finale.
short_description: Railway junctions, medical history, an outdoor lido and food at college.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
transport_note: A town-centre loop starting at the railway station, passing the museum and Lido, and ending on Broadway.

before_you_go.terrain: Town-centre pavements and pedestrian areas, with occasional uneven paving and busy crossings.
before_you_go.hills: Mostly level, with only gentle street gradients.
before_you_go.steps: No steps are required on the intended route; use nearby dropped kerbs at crossings.
before_you_go.accessibility: The checkpoints are outdoors on public routes. Surfaces, temporary works and crowding can vary, so check local access information if step-free travel is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current council, shopping-centre or museum visitor-facility listings before setting off; opening times can change.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable everyday walking shoes should be suitable.
before_you_go.dogs: The outdoor route is suitable for dogs kept under control; check the final venue's current dog policy separately.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Generally suitable for pushchairs, though busy pavements and occasional uneven surfaces may slow progress.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin at the junction that turned a cathedral town into a railway crossroads.
stops.Hint_1: Start on the city-centre side of Peterborough station.
stops.Hint_2: Find the main station entrance and name signs.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Peterborough's first railway station opened in 1850. Competing lines soon made the town an important junction on routes linking London, the north, East Anglia and the Midlands.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the public forecourt, find one sign pointing to more than one railway destination or operator.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Find a grand house that became an infirmary before its rooms filled with local stories.
stops.Hint_1: Walk south-east into the centre towards Priestgate.
stops.Hint_2: Look for the columned museum entrance.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The museum building began as a private house in 1816 and became Peterborough's infirmary in 1857. It later opened as a museum in the twentieth century.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, spot one feature that makes the building look domestic and one that feels institutional.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Seek the open-air pool where interwar Peterborough learned to swim beneath the sky.
stops.Hint_1: Continue east towards Bishop's Road and the riverside parks.
stops.Hint_2: Find the public entrance and Art Deco frontage of the outdoor pool.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Peterborough Lido opened in 1936. Its outdoor pools and streamlined entrance are surviving examples of the interwar enthusiasm for public health, exercise and open-air leisure.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, identify one curved or geometric Art Deco detail.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish in a red-brick school where technical drawing once prepared a city for industry.
stops.Hint_2: Find the food-serving pub in the former college and library buildings.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The older part was built in 1903 as the County Technical College; the adjoining 1906 library was funded by Andrew Carnegie. Check today's hours before stopping for food or a drink.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From the pavement, find the join between the older red-brick sections.
